name: Verb Tense
description: Choosing the correct verb form to express when an action happens (present, past, future, ongoing).
example_errors: She work every day. (missing -s in simple present)
I go to the store yesterday. (present used instead of past)
He will went tomorrow. (mixed future/past marking)

name: Simple Present
description: Used for habits, facts, and routines (e.g. 'She works every day').

name: Simple Past
description: Used for completed actions in the past (e.g. 'She worked yesterday').
example_errors: Yesterday, she go to the store.

name: Simple Future
description: Used for actions expected to happen later, typically with 'will' or 'going to' (e.g. 'She will call tomorrow').

name: Present Continuous
description: Used for actions happening right now or temporarily, formed with 'be' + verb-ing (e.g. 'She is working').

name: Subject-Verb Agreement
description: Matching a verb's form to its subject (e.g. 'She works', not 'She work').

name: Article Usage
description: Choosing between the indefinite articles 'a' and 'an' based on the sound that follows, and knowing when no article or 'the' is needed.

name: Pronouns
description: Using the correct pronoun form depending on its role in the sentence (subject, direct object, indirect object).

name: Direct Object Pronouns
description: Pronouns that receive the action of the verb directly (me, you, him, her, it, us, them).
example_errors: I saw she at the park.
They invited we to the party.

name: Indirect Object Pronouns
description: Pronouns that indicate who benefits from or receives something (e.g. 'Give it to him').
example_errors: She sent a letter to he.

name: Word Order
description: Standard English subject-verb-object order (e.g. 'I eat rice').
example_errors: Yesterday to the store went she.

name: Spelling
description: Correctly spelling common English words, including irregular and frequently-confused forms.

name: Word Choice
description: Choosing the right word for the context, and avoiding missing or extra words that change or obscure meaning.
example_errors: I am agree with you. (extra word 'am')
She very like ice cream. (wrong word order/choice for 'really')
He said me the truth. (wrong word, should be 'told')

name: Everyday Vocabulary
description: Common words used in daily life (e.g. food, family, weather).
example_errors: Using 'umbrella' when the context calls for 'raincoat'.
Using 'make' instead of 'do' for chores (e.g. 'make homework').

name: Main Idea
description: Identifying the central point or purpose of a passage rather than a supporting detail.
example_errors: Picking a minor detail as the passage's main idea.
Choosing an answer that is too broad or unrelated to the passage.
Confusing the topic sentence of one paragraph with the main idea of the whole passage.

name: Detail Retrieval
description: Locating and correctly recalling specific facts stated explicitly in a passage.
example_errors: Reporting a number or name from the passage incorrectly.
Answering with information not actually stated in the passage.
Mixing up which character/subject a detail belongs to.

name: Reading Inference
description: Drawing a reasonable conclusion from information implied, but not directly stated, in a passage.
example_errors: Treating an inference question as if the answer were stated directly.
Drawing a conclusion the passage doesn't actually support.
Ignoring context clues that point to the intended implication.

name: Vocabulary in Context
description: Determining the meaning of a word or phrase from how it's used in the surrounding passage.
example_errors: Using a word's most common meaning when the passage uses a less common one.
Ignoring surrounding context clues that narrow down the meaning.
Confusing a word with a similarly-spelled but unrelated word.
